purpose: Curated capability metadata merged into docs/TOOL_INVENTORY.json by Scripts/generate-tool-inventory.mjs. This file is the ONLY hand-maintained input: canonical capability names, migration actions, C++ builder ownership, and live evidence. Everything countable is derived by the generator; do not record counts here.

verification.live_verified: proven against a live UE4.27 editor by the referenced evidence
verification.live_partial: implemented and exercised live, but the recorded evidence is incomplete (see notes)
verification.pending_live: compiled and unit-tested; the live acceptance has not passed yet
verification.mock_only: unit-tested against the mock listener only
verification.untested: no test of any kind on record

migration_action.KEEP: current implementation remains the supported path for now
migration_action.REFRONT: existing C++ implementation kept; Python/HTTP doorway replaced by the native pipe
migration_action.PORT: no reusable implementation exists; rebuild via the layer named in notes
migration_action.MERGE: narrow tool folded into the stronger canonical capability named in replacement_tool
migration_action.ALIAS: old public name routed to the canonical native tool (compat router)
migration_action.RETIRE: removal proposed; requires evidence, replacement, compatibility coverage, and human sign-off

entry_points: runtime play-test agent module: move, look, press, observe, record, replay

actors.notes: layer: direct_reflection or new_native_wrapper per tool

blueprint-graph.notes: idempotent graph patching is the deferred capability; mutator library is compiled and callable

cpp.notes: belongs to a future build/commandlet backend; legacy lane is the only owner today

effects.notes: layer: direct_reflection for post-process volumes and console effects

intelligence.notes: layer: puerts_workflow; no editor mutation involved

materials.notes: layer: new_native_wrapper; a generic material graph builder is a known gap (sky demo is not one)

optimization.notes: 24-tool profiling suite with no native equivalent; migrate late, by capability group

puerts_blueprint_graph_patch.notes: promoted 2026-08-02 after warm and cold live acceptance passed in full. Incremental patching: named operations against resolved selectors, no clear_existing_graph. Shares the node-creation primitive with puerts_blueprint_build (SpawnNodeFromSpec) so an added node is identical to a built one. Proven on a 22-node fixture: a pin default, an added node with two links, a moved node, a removed node and a disconnect-reconnect pair applied in one batch; every node the patch did not name is structurally identical afterwards; a rerun applies nothing, reports converged and does not save; an ambiguous selector is refused by name without mutating; a batch with one unresolvable target applies neither operation; no dirty package and no source-control entry; and the structure hash survives an editor restart.

puerts_blueprint_member_patch.notes: re-front of UBlueprintMutatorLibrary through the native pipe: the member half of incremental Blueprint editing, which blueprint_graph_patch cannot reach and blueprint_build reaches only by restating the whole asset. Eleven operations over variables, functions, interfaces, event dispatchers and components. The mutations are entirely the existing library; the command adds the classify-before-mutate pass (every mutator entry point recompiles, so a half-applied batch is expensive), one rollback boundary, the compile gate, a per-operation independent read-back, and save only after verification. pre_member_hash / post_member_hash are the same value graph_inspect now returns as member_structure_hash_sha1, so a caller verifies against an independent read. Live acceptance passes warm and cold against BridgeInstallTest (2026-08-03), all checks, twice consecutively warm. compile_status is accompanied by compile_warnings and compile_errors off the same FCompilerResultsLog blueprint_build already reported, so UpToDateWithWarnings is readable without opening the editor; a converged batch still compiles, which makes a no-op call the way to read any Blueprint's compiler messages. Finding 0q settled here: add_event_dispatcher created a signature graph without its multicast delegate property, so every later compile warned and the dispatcher was not bindable.

puerts_behavior_tree_inspect.notes: read half of behavior_tree_build; derived node identity (UE4.27 BT nodes have no GUIDs); donor references: ultimateunrealenginemcp@c31ebac MCPAICommands.cpp BuildBTCompositeNodeJson and monolith@e67544c MonolithAIBehaviorTreeActions HandleGetBehaviorTree, design only, MIT

puerts_widget_inspect.notes: read half of widget_build; derived widget identity (UE4.27 UMG widgets have no GUIDs); reports CanvasPanelSlot anchors/offsets/alignment/z_order, named-slot content that panel-child traversal cannot reach, exposed variables, bindings and animations; read-only proven by package_dirty_before/after, unchanged file hash and mtime, and identical structure hash across two reads and across a restart. Extended 2026-08-03 (lane V) with two ADDITIVE fields, both UNCOMPILED: source_property and source_path per binding entry, and an animation_details array beside the unchanged animations string array. The structure hash basis is unchanged (bindings still hash on widget|property|function|kind, animations still hash on name), so the live evidence above still describes the hash this tool produces.

puerts_widget_bind.notes: UNCOMPILED and never run: written in an isolated worktree with no editor and no UBT pass, so even the compile is unproven. Write half of the bindings and is_variable that widget_inspect could already READ and nothing could author, which is what makes a UMG widget show live data rather than a constant. Writes UWidgetBlueprint::Bindings (FDelegateEditorBinding: ObjectName, PropertyName, FunctionName, SourceProperty, SourcePath, MemberGuid, Kind) and UWidget::bIsVariable. UE4.27 drives the delegate named PropertyName+"Delegate", falling back to the bare name for an event delegate, confirmed at Editor/UMGEditor/Private/WidgetBlueprint.cpp:413 and :440; the caller writes "Percent" and the response reports the delegate it resolved to. A property-kind binding needs a non-empty SourcePath or validation falls through to a FunctionName that is not there, so the path is built with FEditorPropertyPath(TArray<FFieldVariant>), the same public constructor the UMG details panel uses at Customizations/UMGDetailCustomizations.cpp:313, and refused with FEditorPropertyPath::Validate, the engine's own check. Everything validates before anything is written; a compile that returns Error restores the captured Bindings array and bIsVariable flags by value and recompiles, because a Blueprint compile is not an undo record. Convergent: satisfied-ness is re-read immediately before each mutation rather than decided at plan time, so an earlier entry in the same batch cannot make a later one report a false no-op. Widget ANIMATIONS are deliberately NOT authorable here: a UWidgetAnimation wraps a UMovieScene, so track and keyframe authoring is Sequencer's data model and belongs with that work, not duplicated here.

puerts_anim_blueprint_inspect.notes: read half of anim_blueprint_build and the reason it can verify rather than assert; docs/REFRONT_MAP.md group 5 listed AnimBlueprintBuilderLibrary as having no independent inspector, and this is it. Reports anim graphs and their nodes, state machines with entry state, states, conduits and inner pose graphs, transitions keyed from->to with crossfade/priority/blend mode, and per transition a condition kind of rule_graph, automatic_time_remaining or none (an automatic remaining-time rule has no rule graph at all, so reporting only the graph would read as a missing condition); plus cached poses with their readers, blend nodes, member variables and a canonical structure hash that excludes tunable values. Derived node identity: the id a build spec wrote is not persisted on the node. C++ is UNCOMPILED in this lane, which owns no build rights; not exercised against an editor.

puerts_anim_montage_inspect.notes: read-only with no write counterpart, and that is the finding rather than an omission: montage sections and notifies are FAnimLinkableElement values that must be re-linked against slot segments, and UE4.27 exposes no atomic operation for rebuilding the NextSectionName chain, so a montage writer could not be failure-atomic. Notifies are read explicitly because UE4.27 declares them UPROPERTY() with no Edit flag and a CPF_Edit reflection walk drops them. C++ is UNCOMPILED in this lane.

puerts_anim_blend_space_inspect.notes: read-only with no write counterpart, for the same shape of reason as the montage reader: UE4.27 rebuilds a blend space's triangulation from its sample set, so a partly applied sample edit leaves a space that interpolates wrong rather than one that fails, and there is no atomic sample-set replacement a writer could be failure-atomic around. Reports the skeleton, all three blend axes (UE4.27 exposes no dimension count, so the class is what tells 1D from 2D) and every sample with animation, position and rate scale. Samples are sorted by position and animation rather than reported in array order, because array order carries no meaning in a blend space, which is what makes the structure hash stable across two reads. C++ is UNCOMPILED in this lane, which owns no build rights; not exercised against an editor.

puerts_anim_blueprint_build.notes: re-front of UAnimBlueprintBuilderLibrary, which docs/REFRONT_MAP.md group 5 rated BLOCKED on four counts. Three are closed at the command layer rather than in the library: the transaction (IsToolMutating), the rollback boundary (FBridgeAssetRollback, the same one the Blueprint, Widget and Behavior Tree builders use), and an independent inspector (anim_blueprint_inspect). The fourth is closed by SPLITTING create from edit rather than by making one command do both: this one is CREATE-ONLY and refuses an asset that already exists, and puerts_anim_blueprint_patch is the edit half. Creating a new asset IS failure-atomic because the only state a failure must undo is state the command created. Compiles through UBlueprintGraphBuilderLibrary::CompileAndReport and returns the result rather than swallowing it, then reads the asset back and requires every requested state and transition before saving. C++ is UNCOMPILED in this lane.

puerts_anim_blueprint_patch.notes: UNCOMPILED and never run. The edit half finding 0t said could not ship, and what unblocked it was not a new mechanism but noticing the existing one: the .uasset on disk IS the content snapshot the rollback boundary needed, so FBridgeContentSnapshot (MCPBridgePuerTS/Private/MCPBridgeContentSnapshot.h) refuses to start unless the asset is saved and clean, and restores with UPackageTools::ReloadPackages. The in-memory alternative (StaticDuplicateObject plus FKismetEditorUtilities::ReplaceBlueprint, which the engine's own Blueprint merge tool uses) was read and rejected: FBlueprintEditorUtils::PostDuplicateBlueprint regenerates every node and variable guid and builds a fresh generated class without carrying the old CDO's values, so that restore would silently drop every variable default and reopen finding 0r from the other end. Convergent through lane W's FAnimBPBuilder::ClearGeneratedGraph; failure-atomic because nothing is written to disk until the compile and the anim_blueprint_inspect read-back both pass, which also means even a FAILED restore leaves a recoverable asset. rollback_succeeded is decided by re-reading the structure hash after the restore, not asserted. Two costs stated in the response rather than hidden: restoring from disk clears the editor's undo history, and structure_hash_sha1 is not promised stable across a rerun because node identity is derived from UObject names a clear-and-rebuild reassigns. Acceptance written and NOT run: Scripts/animbp-patch-atomicity.mjs.

puerts_blackboard_build.notes: UNCOMPILED. The C++ was written and never built: the lane that added it holds no build rights, so nothing here has been through UBT, let alone an editor. Desired-state reconciliation of a whole Blackboard asset: add, update, remove and reparent, which UMCPBridgeAILibrary::AddBlackboardKeys cannot express because it is add-only. That library is deliberately UNCHANGED; this command carries its own key-type mapping rather than editing the live_verified path behavior_tree_build depends on. No key default value parameter exists because UE4.27 has none: FBlackboardEntry holds EntryName, an instanced UBlackboardKeyType, bInstanceSynced and two editor-only strings, confirmed at Engine/Source/Runtime/AIModule/Classes/BehaviorTree/BlackboardData.h. Convergent (a satisfied rerun returns before the mutation section), failure-atomic (FBridgeAssetRollback plus transaction cancel), independently verified (keys re-read off the asset before save). remove_unlisted is opt-in and is why the annotation is destructiveIdempotent: a removed key silently dangles every FBlackboardKeySelector bound to it.

puerts_blackboard_inspect.notes: UNCOMPILED, same lane and same reason. Read half of blackboard_build: keys with type, base class, instance sync, description, category and an inherited flag, the parent chain, the asset's own IsValid verdict, and a structure hash. identity_kind is authored_name rather than derived, which is the opposite of behavior_tree_inspect and is a property of the asset: a blackboard key's NAME is what every selector binds to, so a rename is a different key.

puerts_eqs_inspect.notes: UNCOMPILED. Read half only, and there is NO eqs_build, which is a decision rather than an unfinished job. UEnvironmentQueryGraph::UpdateAsset (Engine/Plugins/AI/EnvironmentQueryEditor/Source/EnvironmentQueryEditor/Private/EnvironmentQueryGraph.cpp:62) opens with Query->GetOptionsMutable().Reset() and rebuilds Options entirely from the editor UEdGraph, so Options is a compiled artifact and not the source of truth. A builder writing Options without authoring the matching graph would pass its own read-back and be silently wiped the next time a human opened the asset, failing convergence and independent verification at once. The response repeats this in build_unsupported_reason. To use EQS from the bridge, author the query by hand and run it from a Behavior Tree with the RunEQS service, which behavior_tree_build already supports.

puerts_nav_inspect.notes: UNCOMPILED. Reads the editor world's navigation configuration: nav system and build state, ANavigationData actors with agent and generation settings (read by reflected name, so a non-Recast nav data reports what it has), supported agents, NavMeshBoundsVolumes and NavModifierVolumes with world-space boxes, and the bounds the nav system actually registered. The registered bounds are a separate list from the volumes on purpose: a volume in an unloaded sublevel is an actor and is not registered, which is the usual cause of a missing navmesh. APIs confirmed in UE4.27 at Runtime/NavigationSystem/Public/NavigationSystem.h (GetNavigationBounds, GetSupportedAgents, GetDefaultNavDataInstance, GetNumRemainingBuildTasks) and NavMesh/NavMeshBoundsVolume.h, NavModifierVolume.h. Adds NavigationSystem to MCPBridgePuerTS.Build.cs.

puerts_nav_query.notes: UNCOMPILED. Batched read-only navmesh queries: project a point, path length and cost and reachability, navmesh raycast, random navigable point. Batched because a placement decision needs several at once. reachable is true only for ENavigationQueryResult::Success and the raw result word is returned beside it, because Fail (no path) and Error or Invalid (query could not be answered) are different faults and collapsing them would report a configuration problem as a layout problem. APIs confirmed in UE4.27: UNavigationSystemV1::ProjectPointToNavigation, GetPathLength, GetPathCost (instance, const), NavigationRaycast and K2_GetRandomLocationInNavigableRadius (static, world context), Runtime/NavigationSystem/Public/NavigationSystem.h. random_point is non-deterministic and the response warns against using it in a comparison.

puerts_ai_perception_build.notes: UNCOMPILED. Desired-state reconciliation of the whole AIPerceptionComponent config on an existing AIController Blueprint: senses, per-sense properties, dominant sense, component created if missing. Six sense config classes confirmed present in UE4.27 (Sight, Hearing, Damage, Touch, Team, Prediction); UAISenseConfig_Blueprint is refused because its user sense class cannot be validated. UAIPerceptionComponent::SensesConfig and DominantSense are protected UPROPERTYs (AIModule/Classes/Perception/AIPerceptionComponent.h:217-223), so the write goes through FArrayProperty reflection and the read through the public GetSensesConfigIterator. Every sense property is checked against the config class by reflected name before anything is written. Transactional, compiled through UBlueprintGraphBuilderLibrary::CompileAndReport, verified by re-reading the component template, saved only after that passes. Convergent: classification compares every spec-named property against the config already on the component with FJsonValue::CompareEqual and returns before the mutation section when nothing differs, so a satisfied rerun costs no compile and no save; the dominant sense is counted as a change in its own right. The Blueprint must already exist and derive from AIController: this configures a controller, blueprint_build creates one.

puerts_ai_controller_inspect.notes: UNCOMPILED. Read half of ai_perception_build plus the controller-to-BT wiring. That wiring is reported as RunBehaviorTree CALL SITES because UE4.27 has no data-driven field for it: AAIController::RunBehaviorTree is UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable) (AIModule/Classes/AIController.h:255-257) and a controller starts a tree by calling it, so the wiring is a UK2Node_CallFunction and the BTAsset pin default is the only thing resolvable at edit time. A pin wired from a variable resolves to nothing and is listed under dynamic_behavior_tree_call_sites rather than guessed at. NOTHING in this lane WRITES that wiring: puerts_blueprint_build already authors the call node. Only components declared in the Blueprint's SimpleConstructionScript are visible; one inherited from a native parent lives on the parent CDO and the response says so.

puerts_scene_inspect.notes: canonical read of the editor's current level: actors with class, world transform, folder, tags, bounds, attachment and components, plus PlayerStarts and structure_hash_sha1. Shares one snapshot definition with scene_batch (Private/MCPBridgeSceneSnapshot.h), for the reason graph_inspect and blueprint_member_patch share MCPBridgeBlueprintMembers.h: a batch that measured convergence with a different reader than the inspector a caller verifies with could report a change the inspector cannot see. Actor identity is observed (object name, unique within a level), not derived. The hash always covers the whole level; an actors filter narrows the report only, because a hash of a filter is a hash of the request. Read-only on the same terms as graph_inspect: absent from IsToolMutating, reports package_dirty_before/after. UNCOMPILED: lane L holds no build rights, so no editor has run this code.

puerts_scene_batch.notes: desired-state level authoring in one transaction, modelled on blueprint_graph_patch and blueprint_member_patch. Two operations, upsert_actor and delete_actor, cover spawn, modify, delete, reparent, folder, tags and reflected properties on actors and on components they already have; lights and post-process/trigger/blocking/nav-mesh-bounds volumes are upsert_actor with a class path and properties rather than tools of their own. Carries the lane A lesson: satisfied-ness is re-evaluated immediately before each mutation, never read from the plan. Trigger volumes enforce the AGENTS.md PlayerStart rule (a volume containing a PlayerStart refuses the batch; inside 1.5x its extent warns) against real GetActorBounds after placement, inside the rollback boundary. Failure cancels the transaction, runs FBridgeAssetRollback over the level package, and decides rollback_succeeded by re-hashing rather than trusting the undo. It never saves: the level is left dirty and puerts_save writes it, which is what lets a failed batch leave nothing on disk. Property writes are gated by AllowedWritableProperties, widened here by name for light shaping, post-process volume settings, box extent and StaticMeshComponent.StaticMesh. Review pass 2026-08-03 fixed three defects in the salvaged draft: (1) GEditor->AddActor calls World->SpawnActor directly and never runs UActorFactoryBoxVolume::PostSpawnActor, so every AVolume subclass (TriggerVolume, BlockingVolume, PostProcessVolume, NavMeshBoundsVolume) was spawned with a null Brush, zero bounds and no collision, which would also have walked through the PlayerStart clearance check reporting a pass that measured nothing; EnsureVolumeBrush now builds the same 200-unit cube the editor places and refuses the operation if it cannot. (2) ResolveOne collapsed 'matched two' into 'matched none', so an ambiguity an earlier operation in the same batch created would make an upsert spawn a third actor and a delete_actor read as satisfied; the match count is now an output and both the satisfied-predicate and the applier refuse on it. (3) FBridgeAssetRollback::PackageFilename appended the .uasset extension unconditionally, which never resolves for a level (.umap); it now asks FPackageName::DoesPackageExist for the real filename first and falls back to the old concat for a package that does not exist yet, so asset builders are unchanged. UNCOMPILED and NOT live: no build rights in this lane, no live acceptance script yet.

puerts_input_mapping_info.notes: the inspector UMCPBridgeInputLibrary never had: the library could add and remove bindings with no reader, so a mutation could only be confirmed by the mutator own report. Read-only: absent from the native IsToolMutating list, const accessors on UInputSettings only. Canonically sorted, reduced to mapping_hash_sha1, which is what input_mapping_patch reports as pre/post hash. NOT COMPILED and NOT run: this lane built no editor.

puerts_input_mapping_patch.notes: re-front of UMCPBridgeInputLibrary behind one reconciling command: the legacy lane spent one round trip per binding across three tools and a control scheme is eleven bindings. The library per-mapping validation and duplicate rejection are reused; the command adds classify-before-write, presets expanded client side, and the boundary the library never had. DefaultInput.ini is not a UObject, so instead of a transaction the command snapshots both mapping arrays, restores them on any failure, and decides rollback_succeeded by re-reading and comparing the hash. NOT COMPILED and NOT run.

puerts_folder_visibility.notes: re-front of UFolderVisibilityLibrary. Display-only Content Browser state in Config/FolderVisibility.ini; hidden folders stay on disk, referenced and cookable. Desired-state hidden converges; hide/show is the delta form; the two shapes are refused together rather than merged. No hidden/hide/show at all is the read, which is what folder_hidden_list asked for. The hidden set in the response is read back from GetHiddenFolders, never echoed. NOT COMPILED and NOT run.

puerts_camera_shake.notes: re-front of UAutoPIEHelper::PlayCameraShakeOnPlayer, which owns the PIE World to PlayerController(0) to PlayerCameraManager chain. Runtime only: nothing persisted, nothing to undo. Refuses by name when PIE is not running rather than reporting a shake nobody could have seen. UE4.27 note: UCameraShakeBase with StartCameraShake, not the older names. NOT COMPILED and NOT run.

puerts_pie_agent_query.notes: the READ-ONLY half of UPIEAgentLibrary: observe, read_property, status, expect. One behaviour difference from the legacy pie_agent_expect: the native command starts the check and returns operation_id rather than blocking until the verdict; poll op=status. The runtime control half is puerts_pie_agent_control. NOT COMPILED and NOT run.

puerts_pie_agent_control.notes: One user-gated native command re-fronts all nine existing UPIEAgentLibrary control operations: move_to, look_at, press, key_state, axis_state, clear_axes, record_start, record_stop and replay. Runtime-only and intentionally outside editor transactions. It never starts PIE. Editor-free schema, annotation and dispatch coverage pass. UBT and final DLL linking pass in BridgeInstallTest; install:check is green. NOT run live.

puerts_material_inspect.notes: the read half material authoring never had, for UMaterial and UMaterialInstanceConstant at one tool name; observed expression identity (a material expression's UObject name is unique in its package and is serialized, unlike a UMG widget or a BT node); canonical structure hash over the parameter set, override flags, expressions and links, values excluded so retinting an instance does not read as a reshape. For master material GRAPHS this is the only half: UMaterialEditingLibrary::CreateMaterialExpressionEx (MaterialEditingLibrary.cpp:469) and ConnectMaterialExpressions (:631) both write without calling Modify, so a failed multi-node build cannot be rolled back and no write command was shipped. NOT compiled and NOT run: the lane that added this launched no editor.

puerts_material_instance_build.notes: re-front of UMaterialEditingLibrary's material instance setters plus the boundary that library does not have: the /Game/MCPGenerated/ limit, whole-request validation against the parent before any asset is created, Modify() so the writes are in the undo record at all (the library's setters call SetScalarParameterValueEditorOnly and friends without it, MaterialEditingLibrary.cpp:966/:987/:1008, which also return a hardcoded false), one rollback boundary, a compile whose result is reported rather than assumed, an independent read-back that decides whether the writes landed, and a save only after that read-back passes. compile.instance_own_resource distinguishes the instance's own static permutation from the parent's inherited resource, so a parent's pre-existing compile errors are not blamed on this request. NOT compiled and NOT run: the lane that added this launched no editor.

puerts_material_build.notes: UNCOMPILED. The C++ was written and never built: the lane that added it holds no build rights, so nothing here has been through UBT, let alone an editor. Authors a whole UMaterial graph from a desired-state spec: expression nodes, named scalar/vector/texture/static-switch parameters, node-to-node links, and links into BaseColor, EmissiveColor, Roughness, Normal and the rest. This REPLACES the read-only verdict material_instance_build shipped with. That verdict rested on UMaterialEditingLibrary::CreateMaterialExpressionEx (MaterialEditingLibrary.cpp:469) adding to UMaterial::Expressions with no Material->Modify(), and ConnectMaterialExpressions (:631) writing through FExpressionInput::Connect the same way - both confirmed here. What it missed is that the engine's own material editor has the same problem and owns Modify() at the call site: FMaterialEditor::CreateNewMaterialExpression (MaterialEditor.cpp:4344) opens an FScopedTransaction, calls Material->Modify(), then calls CreateMaterialExpressionEx. UObject::Modify (Obj.cpp:1206) forwards to SaveToTransactionBuffer (UObjectGlobals.cpp:2197), which calls GUndo->SaveObject - a serialized pre-mutation snapshot - so one Modify() puts the Expressions array and the material's own FExpressionInput members in the undo record. That covers the material and not a pre-existing expression's own inputs, so this command never rewrites one: FULL GRAPH REPLACEMENT means every expression it connects is one it created inside the same transaction, and the UMaterial is the only pre-existing object it mutates. Old expressions are dropped from the array and deliberately NOT marked pending kill, so a cancel restores pointers to live objects. Modify()'s return value is CHECKED and the command refuses before writing anything if it is false, because finding 0r is what a discarded Modify() result costs. Rollback is verified by re-reading: the Asset Registry on a create, the structure hash on a replace. Compile result reported rather than assumed; save only after an independent read-back through the material_inspect reader agrees every link, material output and parameter landed. Bypasses CreateMaterialExpressionEx and ConnectMaterialExpressions entirely (NewObject plus Expressions.Add plus FExpressionInput::Connect, the same path puerts_sky_shader_create already takes) so the Modify() ownership is explicit rather than buried in a library call. destructiveIdempotent: the spec is the whole graph.

puerts_texture_import.notes: UNCOMPILED. The C++ was written and never built. Closes the gap docs/GAP_AUDIT-2026-07-29.md recorded as no texture tools at all: material_instance_build accepts a textures map and material_build accepts a texture parameter default, and nothing could produce a texture for either. GENERATES a solid colour or checker UTexture2D rather than importing from disk. FTextureSource::Init(W,H,1,1,TSF_BGRA8,bytes) with PostEditChange building the platform mip chain, the same shape FImageUtils::CreateTexture2D uses for a colour buffer. File import is deliberately absent rather than half-built: it needs an allowed import root this bridge does not define, engine_source_read's engine root is for reading engine source and not user content, and inventing a second filesystem trust root is a decision for the integrator. A spec naming source_file is refused by name with that reason. Convergent by construction: the same spec produces identical source bytes, so a rerun memcmps equal, reports unchanged, opens no write and dirties nothing. Modify() return value checked, source pixels read back and compared byte for byte before any save. Size is capped at 2048 and restricted to powers of two because generation runs on the game thread. sRGB changes the bytes written (FLinearColor::ToFColor) rather than only a flag, and defaults from the compression choice so a Normalmap is not silently gamma encoded.

puerts_lighting_build.notes: starts a Lightmass build for the level the editor has open, or reports the state of one. IT DOES NOT WAIT: UEditorEngine::BuildLighting hands the level to FStaticLightingManager and returns, and the build then advances on UpdateBuildLighting from the editor tick over minutes; a command that blocked on that would sit far past any request budget this bridge allows, and a timeout reported while the editor kept building is wrong in both directions. So action=start returns waited:false with a completion note, and action=status is the poll. started is read back from IsLightingBuildCurrentlyRunning rather than assumed, because CreateStaticLightingSystem returns void and swallows a refused start; bForceNoPrecomputedLighting and r.AllowStaticLighting=0 are refused by name first. Refused during PIE: Lightmass reads GWorld. ADDITIVE CHANGE (lane Z): action=start now also returns a job_id and the build is registered on the job API, so it can be polled with puerts_job_status and CANCELLED with puerts_job_cancel; action=status additionally reports the live job id. No parameter was renamed and no behaviour changed. The earlier claim here that UE4.27 exposes no public abort was wrong: GEditor->SetMapBuildCancelled is public (EditorEngine.h:816, overridden UnrealEdEngine.h:201) and is what the editor own cancel button reaches. The start path now clears that flag first, as EditorBuildUtils.cpp:248 does, because it is a single global flag and a leftover true would abort every later build. UNCOMPILED: lane U holds no build rights, so no editor has run this code.

puerts_job_status.notes: UNCOMPILED. Reports the state of one job, or lists every job this editor session holds. A job is work the ENGINE advances while the game thread is free, which is the only kind this bridge can track: UEditorEngine::BuildLighting hands the level to FStaticLightingManager and returns while the build advances on the editor tick (StaticLightingSystem.cpp:2492-2522, :341-386); ANavigationData::RebuildAll does not block (NavigationData.h:619); a sequence render is a second process. Between slices of all three the game thread is free, so this is an ordinary short command and needs no second pipe, no FTicker and no chunked executor - none of docs/PERF_AND_LONG_JOBS.md 6.5 changes 1 to 3 was made. Nothing is cached: every live counter is derived at poll time from the engine or the OS, and there is deliberately no percent, because no UE4.27 entry point on any of these paths reports a fraction. Job ids carry the session id that minted them, so an id from a previous editor answers job_lost_editor_restarted rather than being reported as running.

puerts_job_result.notes: UNCOMPILED. Delivers a finished job output ONCE. The starting command answer is retained on the job record, so it outlives the command that produced it and a client that lost it can still read it. Refuses with job_still_running before the job finishes and job_result_consumed on a second call, rather than answering with a stale or empty body. Collecting drops the record, and the map is capped at 32 with the oldest FINISHED records evicted first; a running job is never evicted.

puerts_job_cancel.notes: UNCOMPILED. Cancellation is per job kind and the response says which, because a cancel that returns success and does nothing is worse than no cancel. immediate for a sequence render only (FPlatformProcess::TerminateProc on the second process). deferred for a lighting build: GEditor->SetMapBuildCancelled is public in 4.27 (EditorEngine.h:816, overridden UnrealEdEngine.h:201) and is what the editor own cancel button reaches (StaticLightingSystem.cpp:182-193 via SBuildProgress.cpp:212), and Lightmass reads the flag between units of work (Lightmass.cpp:726, :1312, :3385, :3479) so the build stops at its NEXT check. deferred for a navigation build: UNavigationSystemV1::CancelBuild is public (NavigationSystem.h:823) and the queued Recast tile tasks unwind. This CORRECTS the previous claim that Lightmass exposes no public abort; the cancel button proves otherwise. It cannot interrupt an engine call already in progress, so puerts_nav_build with wait:true gets no job id at all. Nothing is rolled back: a cancelled navmesh is partial and a cancelled render keeps the frames it wrote. lighting_build start now clears the flag first (as EditorBuildUtils.cpp:248 does), without which one cancel would poison every later build in the session.

puerts_sequence_render_start.notes: UNCOMPILED, and the command finding 0s said could not ship synchronously. It ships asynchronously instead, on the job API. Legacy MovieSceneCapture in a second process, the same path the editor own Render Movie button takes in separate-process mode: a UAutomatedLevelSequenceCapture is built and serialized with the engine own converter, written to a per-render manifest under Saved/MCPPuerTSBridge, and a second editor process is launched with -MovieSceneCaptureManifest (MovieSceneCaptureDialogModule.cpp:678-744). Movie Render Queue exists in 4.27 at Engine/Plugins/MovieScene/MovieRenderPipeline and is EnabledByDefault false, so it is not used. The manifest is produced from the real UObject rather than hand-written JSON because the child reconstructs it with FJsonObjectConverter::JsonAttributesToUStruct (MovieSceneCaptureModule.cpp:104-160). The refusals are the work: the second process reads the level and the sequence FROM DISK, so an unsaved or never-saved level and an unsaved sequence are refused by name rather than producing a correct-looking render of the previous version; PIE is refused; the output directory must resolve inside the project. Needs the MovieSceneCapture and MovieSceneTools module dependencies. Opens no transaction and touches no asset: it writes image files, so there is nothing to undo.

puerts_project_settings_maps.notes: UNCOMPILED. Native re-front of the legacy project_settings_maps request shape. Validates existing saved /Game maps and a resolvable GameModeBase class before mutation, writes the UGameMapsSettings CDO through UE4.27 APIs, persists DefaultEngine.ini with UpdateDefaultConfigFile, reads back, and restores previous values on a mismatch. Requires editor-free typecheck plus UHT, UBT and warm/cold config proof.

puerts_project_package_start.notes: UNCOMPILED. Starts fixed RunUAT BuildCookRun in a child process and returns a job id without waiting. Caller input is limited to 1..32 existing saved /Game maps, Win64, Development or Shipping, and an archive directory contained by Project/Saved. Project and RunUAT paths are derived, dirty packages and PIE are refused, stdout/stderr is retained as a bounded tail, and cancellation terminates only the owned process tree while preserving partial output. This packages a game project and never invokes the known-blocked UE4.27 BuildPlugin binary path. UHT, UBT and live UAT success/cancel proof remain outstanding.

puerts_class_defaults_patch.notes: sets inherited class-default (CDO) values on a generated Blueprint, which blueprint_build has no section for: AIControllerClass and AutoPossessAI are the gap the AI slice hit, and both are added to AllowedWritableProperties by name. A variable the Blueprint itself declares is refused and pointed at blueprint_member_patch, whose set_variable_default writes the FBPVariableDescription default as well as the CDO. The transaction is deliberately not the rollback: finding 0r measured that UObject::Modify does nothing for a non-RF_Transactional object and a CDO is one, so this command snapshots the exported text of every property it will touch, restores it on failure, decides rollback_succeeded by reading the values again, and reports Modify() return value as transaction_covers_cdo. Convergence is decided by comparing two exported strings produced by the same import-and-export path, on a scratch copy, so an invalid value is rejected before the CDO is touched. UNCOMPILED: lane U holds no build rights, so no editor has run this code.

puerts_sequence_inspect.notes: the first tool in this bridge that touches Sequencer at all. Reads a ULevelSequence as canonical JSON: display rate, tick resolution, playback range, possessables and spawnables, master and object tracks, sections with their ranges and row indices, and every key on every channel with its time, value and interpolation. Read-only: absent from IsToolMutating, nothing calls Modify or MarkPackageDirty, package_dirty_before/after reported. Binding identity is OBSERVED - the FGuid UMovieScene already stores - unlike the derived identities widget_inspect and behavior_tree_inspect must use. Frames are reported in DISPLAY-RATE frames with the raw ticks beside them, so a caller never has to know the 60000-per-second tick resolution; the conversion is FFrameRate::TransformTime, the engine's own integer path. Canonical order is bindings by name then guid, tracks by binding then type then property, sections by start tick then row, channels in engine channel order. structure_hash_sha1 comes from MCPBridgeBlueprintMembers::StructureHash - the same digest and the same lowercase hex the graph, Behavior Tree, widget and scene inspectors report - and covers keyframe VALUES as well as shape, because for a sequence a key value is the content. Actor resolution is reported under 'resolution' and is deliberately OUTSIDE the hashed set: it depends on which level the editor has open, not on the asset. UNCOMPILED and NOT live: this lane had no build rights and no editor.

puerts_sequence_build.notes: desired-state ULevelSequence authoring in one transaction: display rate, playback range, possessable and spawnable bindings, Transform/Float/Bool/Visibility/Camera tracks, sections and keyframes. Modelled on scene_batch and blueprint_graph_patch. Carries the lane A lesson explicitly: every binding, track, section and key asks the live UMovieScene whether it is already satisfied immediately before its own mutation, and no verdict is read from a plan - the playback-range tick conversion in particular happens AFTER the display-rate change in the same call, because converting it earlier would use the rate the sequence had rather than the one it now has. ADDITIVE by design: no remove_unlisted, no clear_existing, nothing is deleted, and that is a stated gap rather than a half-built feature. Failure-atomic: the whole spec is validated before an asset exists (actor labels resolved to exactly one actor, classes loaded and checked against AActor, track types and properties checked, duplicate track identities refused), and any later refusal cancels the transaction, runs FBridgeAssetRollback, and decides rollback_succeeded by re-hashing rather than trusting the undo. Verified by an independent re-read: after applying, every track, section and key is looked up again in the asset as it now is. Four UE4.27 facts this depends on, each confirmed in D:/UE/UE_4.27/Engine/Source: a transform section is nine FMovieSceneFloatChannel (FMovieSceneDoubleChannel does not exist in 4.27); rotation channel order is Roll/Pitch/Yaw at indices 3/4/5, not FRotator member order; the camera binding is UE::MovieScene::FRelativeObjectBindingID, not the removed three-argument FMovieSceneObjectBindingID; and ULevelSequence::BindPossessableObject is a SILENT no-op on a null Context, which the command refuses rather than discovers at playback. ULevelSequenceFactoryNew is private to the LevelSequenceEditor plugin and cannot be included, so creation reproduces its five lines. Needs the LevelSequence, MovieScene and MovieSceneTracks module dependencies, all Runtime. UNCOMPILED and NOT live.

puerts_nav_build.notes: UNCOMPILED. The write half of the navigation group, closing it beside nav_inspect and nav_query. Rebuilds the editor world navigation so a placed NavMeshBoundsVolume produces an actual navmesh. MUTATING and deliberately NOT transactional, and absent from IsToolMutating for that reason: navmesh tiles are derived data generated by background tasks into a generator the transaction buffer does not record, and UE4.27 own Build Paths calls GEditor->ResetTransaction("Rebuilding Navigation") before triggering the same build (Editor/UnrealEd/Private/EditorBuildUtils.cpp:395), discarding the undo stack outright, so a transaction here would record an undo entry that restores nothing. Not destructive: navigation data is derived from the level, so the recovery from a bad build is another build. Independently inspected by calling InspectNavigationJson for the read-back, the same function puerts_nav_inspect uses, so the two cannot disagree. Two shapes because of time: wait defaults to false and calls the public non-blocking ANavigationData::RebuildAll (Runtime/NavigationSystem/Public/NavigationData.h:619) on every registered nav data, answering status building for the caller to poll nav_inspect until remaining_build_tasks is zero; wait true calls FNavigationSystem::Build (Runtime/Engine/Classes/AI/NavigationSystemBase.h:167), which is what FEditorBuildUtils::TriggerNavigationBuilder does (EditorBuildUtils.cpp:868) and which BLOCKS until every nav data returns from EnsureBuildCompletion (Runtime/NavigationSystem/Private/NavigationSystem.cpp:3329-3335), so on a large level it outlasts the 30s pipe deadline while the build keeps running in the editor. Only the blocking path spawns a missing RecastNavMesh, because UNavigationSystemV1::SpawnMissingNavigationData is protected (NavigationSystem.h:1098, under the protected: at 1024), so wait false refuses a level with bounds volumes and no nav data actor and names wait true as the fix. Every precondition is refused by name BEFORE any generator runs, because UNavigationSystemV1::Build RETURNS SILENTLY when it has no work (NavigationSystem.cpp:3297-3302) and a command that called it blind would report a successful build over a level that still has no navmesh: no navigation system, no NavMeshBoundsVolume, IsNavigationBuildingLocked with the editor auto-update flag masked out exactly as Build masks it (NavigationSystem.h:831, ENavigationBuildLock at :88), and IsThereAnywhereToBuildNavigation false (NavigationSystem.h:605). plan_only runs every precondition and no generator. ADDITIVE CHANGE (lane Z): the wait false path now also returns a job_id, so the started-not-finished shape it already had is pollable with puerts_job_status and cancellable with puerts_job_cancel (UNavigationSystemV1::CancelBuild, NavigationSystem.h:823). wait true returns an EMPTY job_id on purpose: it blocked inside the generator, which is the one shape the job API cannot cover. plan_only returns an empty job_id too. No parameter was renamed and no behaviour changed. NOT COMPILED and NOT run: this lane holds no build rights and no editor has executed this code.

puerts_audio_build.notes: Desired-state UE4.27 Sound Cue authoring under /Game/MCPGenerated. Supports Wave Player, Mixer, Random, Modulator, Delay, Looping and Concatenator nodes, stable ids, ordered child links, Sound Wave references and reflected editable properties. Validates the full tree and property conversion on transient objects before mutation. Existing cues require a saved clean package and use FBridgeContentSnapshot; new cues use FBridgeAssetRollback. USoundCue::FirstNode and USoundNode::ChildNodes remain the playable truth, and LinkGraphNodesFromSoundNodes derives the editor graph. Every successful mutation is read back through audio_inspect before save. plan_only and convergent reruns do not write. TypeScript contract, UHT, UE4.27 C++ compile, library creation, DLL link and install parity pass. Warm, cold and user-authorized PIE playback evidence remain outstanding.

puerts_audio_inspect.notes: Native read-back for Sound Cues and Sound Waves. Reports common USoundBase fields and every EditAnywhere property. For Sound Cues it walks FirstNode and ordered ChildNodes, reports stable node ids, classes, titles, reflected properties, explicit Sound Wave references and a canonical structure_hash_sha1. It also warns about a missing FirstNode and orphaned AllNodes. This is the independent verifier for puerts_audio_build. Read only, absent from IsToolMutating, and package dirty state is measured before and after. TypeScript contract, UHT, UE4.27 C++ compile, library creation, DLL link and install parity pass. Live warm and cold evidence remains outstanding.

puerts_cloth_inspect.notes: UNCOMPILED. REFRONT of MCPBridgeClothOptimizer, read half only. Straight pass-through to UClothOptimizerLibrary::InspectClothAsset (Public/ClothOptimizerLibrary.h:20), which the module's own SClothOptimizerPanel also reads, so an MCP read and what a human sees in the panel are one function's output rather than two implementations that can disagree. The command adds path resolution (a bare package path grows its asset name, because the library loads by object path), the standard envelope, and one lift: the library reports its own failures INSIDE the snapshot as success:false with an error string rather than by returning nothing, so an unsuccessful read is raised to a refusal instead of being passed through as a success envelope carrying success:false, which is the shape a caller is least likely to check. A mesh with no clothAssets is answered with a warning naming it as a mesh with no cloth, not refused. WRITE HALF DELIBERATELY NOT FRONTED, per docs/REFRONT_MAP.md group 3: ApplyFabricProfile, SmoothMaxDistanceTransition and ApplyLowerLegGradient open an FScopedTransaction and never cancel it on the failure path, and what they mutate is cloth PAINT, authored data a re-run cannot regenerate, so a half-applied mask is lost work rather than lost time. They ship when a failed apply provably restores the mask; until then cloth_apply_fabric_profile, cloth_smooth_max_distance and cloth_apply_lower_leg_gradient stay on the legacy listener with their confirm parameter. write_unsupported_reason says so in every response. READ ONLY: absent from IsToolMutating, nothing calls Modify or MarkPackageDirty. Reports one package_dirty_after_read flag rather than a before/after pair, because InspectClothAsset loads the mesh itself and there is no moment at which this command could observe the package before the read. NOT COMPILED and NOT run: this lane holds no build rights.
